title: Black Older Adults’ Perception of Using Voice Assistants to Enact a Medical Recovery Curriculum

bias_targets.methodology: Participatory design (focus groups and speed-dating sessions) to elicit Black older adults' feedback on cultural relevance, IVA accents, media representation, and systemic healthcare disparities.
Qualitative analysis of older adults' reactions to voice-assistant care scenarios to identify stigmas associated with aging and the conflation of age with frailty.
Thematic analysis of participants' perceptions of an adaptive medical recovery curriculum, revealing stigmas around physical limitations and the reluctance to identify as needing assistance.
Analyzing participant feedback regarding the affordability of the technology, internet access barriers (digital redlining), and the educational accessibility of the IVA's reading content.
Evaluating qualitative reactions to visual and conceptual design metaphors (e.g., digital gardens versus sports analogies) to identify assumptions around traditional gender norms and preferences.
